title: Change approval orchestration for canary & shadow rollouts
creator: Sofia Torres
description:
Problem: Teams deploying model variants (canary, A/B, and shadow) currently rely on ad-hoc Slack approvals and manual runbooks. This creates inconsistent gating, missing audit trails, and slow incident response when a model causes regressions. Goal: Ship a standardized, auditable approval orchestration that integrates RBAC, required sign-offs, and automated rollback triggers for production model rollouts (canary/A-B/shadow). The feature should be usable across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and exposed in Redwood Console, CLI, and API.

Scope:
- Approval gates that can be attached to rollout policies (canary percentage stages, A/B experiments, shadow mirroring).
- Role-based permission model for who can approve/override (PM, SRE, Security, Legal).
- Persisted audit logs with immutable records (actor, timestamp, decision, rationale, linked PR/CR/Change request).
- Automatic enforcement: a rollout cannot progress past a gate without approvals unless explicitly allowed by an override policy and RBAC.
- Auto-rollback hooks: metric-based triggers (latency, error-rate, quality regressions) that can abort/rollback in-flight canaries and surface required postmortems.
- Console UX: pending approval UI, sign-off checklist, and history view per rollout.
- API + CLI for programmatic automation and CD integrations.

Non-goals: complex multi-org approval hierarchies, full ITIL change calendar integration (can be future integration point).
acceptance_criteria: Define RBAC roles and permissions for approval actions and overrides and document them in the Security page.
Approval gate can be attached to a canary or A/B rollout policy with configurable required approvers (min N and role types).
Console displays pending gates with clear list of required approvers and an action to approve/reject with a comment. Approvals produce immutable audit entries.
API returns rollout state including gate metadata and audit log entries.
Auto-rollback executes when any configured metric crosses its threshold for the configured evaluation window and posts a linked incident and rollback audit entry.
Shadow traffic mode can be enabled with optional approval (for initial experiments) and logs request/response diffs for flagged regressions.
E2E test coverage for approval flow and rollback path in runtime-1.20 release branch.
design_notes: RBAC model will be additive on top of existing org/team membership. Proposed roles: rollout_admin, rollout_approver, rollout_viewer, security_reviewer. Detailed mapping in design doc (Confluence).
Approval gates are first-class objects attached to RolloutPolicies; they support a min_approvers integer and allowed_roles list. The Console will surface both required roles and named approvers.

Audit logs are stored in the existing audit-index with new schema fields: action_type, gate_id, rationale, linked_pr, pre_snapshot_hash. Retention defaults to 365 days for Hosted; expose export for Dedicated/Private customers.

Rollback triggers: support metric expressions (e.g., error_rate > 1.0% AND p99_latency > baseline*1.2) evaluated over a sliding window. These expressions will be compiled and sent to the evaluation service in the runtime.
Console UX: compact gate card in the Rollouts page, modal to approve with comment and optional file upload (link to CR). Sign-off history view includes diff links to GitHub PRs.
rollout_steps: 1) Add Approval Gate object type in backend and wire basic CRUD API (pm/eng).
2) Implement RBAC checks in rollout execution path to pause on gate; deny progression without approval tokens.
3) Build Console UI: pending gates view + approval modal + history. (Design review scheduled).
4) Implement audit log persistence and export endpoints.
5) Hook metric-based auto-rollback: evaluator service integration and standard metric templates.
6) Add CLI/API calls for programmatic approvals and a webhook for external CD systems.
7) QA: canary experiments with synthetic traffic and chaos tests to validate rollback behavior.
8) Docs: runbook for on-call, example sign-off templates, and security review checklist.
